subject: research/selfrep-recyclers
professional: a polymer-recycling / distributed-manufacturing engineer who has built or specified a shredder-extruder filament line (the Recyclebot / Precious Plastic community), plus a metals-casting practitioner for the aluminium furnace; first checks: is the machine BOM a real design, does the extruder line make usable diameter-controlled filament, and can remelted offcuts actually replace sheet stock

evidence.correctness: Ran `python3 experiments/run.py`; output is byte-identical to the committed experiments/results.txt. Recomputed by hand from the BOM files (not from the code under audit): (1) printer-copy plastic P = 44 printed parts x 25 g = 1.10 kg, F = P/0.9 = 1.222 kg, own-scrap saving = r*s*F = 0.8*0.1*1.222 = 0.0978 kg/copy (reported 0.098). (2) Plastic-pair imports in printer+cnc+laser: vitamins 3.448+1.520 = 4.968 kg, MDF (3.0+1.0)/0.7 = 5.714 kg, filament 0.6/0.9 = 0.667 kg, total 11.349 kg; /0.0978 = 116.1 copies (reported 116); printer-only 9.637/0.0978 = 98.6 (reported 99). (3) Furnace: Al product = 100x1.5+50x0.1+2x10 = 175 g, offcut = 175*(1/0.7-1) = 75 g, remelt saving 0.92*75 = 0.069 kg; 6.5/0.069 = 94.2 (reported 94). (4) eol=1, phi=0.8: pool = 0.1222+1.1 = 1.222, 0.8*pool = 0.978 = phi*F, payback 11.35/0.978 = 11.6 (reported 12); phi=0.3 saving = 0.3F = 0.367, payback 30.9 (reported 31). (5) Monte Carlo re-implemented independently with a different seed (12345, 20000 draws, 14 independent log-uniform factors): 5/50/95% = 92/124/165 vs reported 91/123/164. All arithmetic reproduces. Capped at 2 because (a) every driving input (machine masses, part lists, y_metal applied to MDF, 8% melt loss) is an invented placeholder although real open BOMs exist, and (b) the furnace output (94 copies) rests on remelted offcuts substituting for imported aluminium sheet/bar, which a crucible furnace cannot produce (no rolling or extrusion; it makes ingots/castings); thin-sheet offcuts also lose far more than 8% to dross. The number is right for the model, not for the physical question.
evidence.completeness: Checked every README claim against results.txt: 99/116 copies (yes), 9.6 and 11.4 kg imports (yes), 91-164 median 123 (yes), furnace 94 and 67-144/100 (yes), 31 at phi=0.3 and 12 at phi=0.8 (yes), 24-44 (yes), vitamins 5.0/9.0 kg vs printer copy 4.9-5.3 kg (yes: 4.968, 8.97 vs vitamin_mass 4.935-5.26 recomputed). Tests: 8 as stated. Figure script runs and regenerates payback.svg with no diff. Card present in _homepage/projects.json and research/README.md. No stubs or TODOs. The stated next steps (cost weighting, endogenous eol, folding into closure) were partly done by a sibling project already.
evidence.verification: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`: 8 tests, OK. Seeded mutations in src/selfrep_recyclers/machines.py, each reverted with git checkout (git status clean for the project afterwards): (M1) payback `imp / pl` changed to `imp * pl`: caught (test_payback_shrinks_with_retired_plastic fails). (M2) filament feedstock `m / (1 - s)` changed to `m * (1 - s)`: caught (test_import_at_least_mass). (M4) furnace branch disabled: caught. (M3) sheet yield dropped, `m / y_metal` changed to `m`, which shrinks the plastic-pair imports from 11.35 to ~9.6 kg and moves the headline payback 116 -> ~98: NOT caught, all 8 tests pass. No test asserts any absolute payback, import mass or the Monte Carlo quantiles, and nothing checks results.txt against a rerun, so the headline numbers are guarded only by order relations.
evidence.craft: Read machines.py, tests/test_recyclers.py, experiments/run.py. Clean 114-line module, docstrings state the assumptions, dataclass reuse from selfrep-closure. Defects: sys.path.insert hacks into two sibling trees (works only from this repo layout); run.py monkey-patches the module-global MACHINES dict and rebuilds Part objects positionally (breaks silently if Part gains a field); machine_mass_kg has an unused variant_scale parameter; unused `import M` and `PLASTIC_PAIR` re-imports in run.py; machine_import_kg applies the aluminium/metal cutting yield y_metal to MDF sheet without saying so in the docstring; paybacks() returns None for zero saving but run.py is the only caller that formats it. Tests import SHOPS through machines (re-export), fragile.
evidence.claims: Every number in the README and the homepage summary traces to results.txt and reproduces (see completeness). Limitations are honest and prominent: assumed inputs, mass as sole currency, retirement as a scenario knob, no wear parts. The 'Stylised' label is disclosed with the inputs that are unsourced. Weaknesses: the README says no published shredder/extruder design is reproduced and lists 'replace with a real open design' as an OWNER step, but open BOMs exist and the repo's own research/CLAUDE.md ('Run the numbers; don't stylise them') says to cite findable parameters at point of use; the Builds-on section cites no recycling literature at all. No claim is false.
evidence.fitness: Walked the researcher's job: reproduce (works, stdlib only), vary a part mass (easy), swap in a real shredder BOM (possible but every number must be hand-typed into MACHINES). Nearest prior work, from memory and not re-fetched in this session: Pearce group distributed-recycling papers (Baechler, DeVuono and Pearce 2013, Rapid Prototyping Journal, the 'Recyclebot'; Kreiger et al. 2014, life-cycle analysis of distributed polymer recycling, Journal of Cleaner Production), the Precious Plastic open machine designs, and the RepRap closure and von Neumann/Freitas-Merkle line the README does cite. Those works give measured energy and cost payback of shredder-extruder systems; none is cited, and none is compared against. The idea of counting the recyclers' own imported mass against avoided imports is, to my knowledge, not stated that way in that literature, so the framing is plausibly new, but the result ('about 100 copies on own scrap') is a consequence of placeholder masses and a 0.1 kg/copy scrap assumption, so it is not a finding a researcher can build on until it is rerun on a real BOM. It is a small milestone rather than a programme step toward a named venue.
evidence.domain: A recycling engineer would object first that the extruder line has no puller, cooling bath, diameter gauge or fan, so it cannot make 1.75 mm filament within tolerance; that a 3 kg-class geared shredder motor plus 6x150 g cutter plates is a guess; and that recycled-filament quality (phi) is decisive and unmeasured (the project says so). A metals practitioner would object that remelted washer/pulley offcuts cannot become the imported 'aluminium sheet' or 'bar' (needs rolling/extrusion), and that dross on thin offcuts is typically well above 8%. Mass-only payback also treats MDF and motors alike, flagged in limitations and addressed by the sibling cost project. Method structure (feedstock/yield/scrap/phi cap) is sound and the sensitivity is honest about covering mass only. Departs from practice in using no measured data.

defects.what: Furnace payback (94 copies, repeated in README and homepage) credits remelted offcuts as replacing imported aluminium sheet/bar, which a crucible furnace cannot make; dross assumed 8% for thin offcuts. The headline furnace number is not physically supported.
Mutation that removes the sheet cutting yield from machine_import_kg (headline plastic payback 116 -> ~98) passes all 8 tests; no test pins an absolute payback or compares to results.txt.

Machine part lists and masses are invented although real open shredder/extruder designs with bills of materials exist; no recycling literature (Recyclebot, Precious Plastic) is cited or compared, contrary to research/CLAUDE.md 'Run the numbers'.
Extruder BOM omits puller, cooling and diameter control; sensitivity scales masses only, not the parts list; y_metal reused for MDF undocumented.
Dead parameter variant_scale, unused imports, positional Part reconstruction and global-dict monkey-patching in run.py.

verdict: The arithmetic is right and reproducible: five outputs recomputed by hand from the BOM files (0.098 kg/copy saving, 11.35 kg import, 116 and 99 copies, 94 furnace copies, 31 and 12 with retired plastic) and an independent Monte Carlo with another seed gave 92/124/165 against the reported 91/123/164. The README is candid that everything is assumed and mass-only, and every claim traces to results.txt, so it is finished and honestly labelled. It does not meet the bar: tests are order checks only and a mutation that moves the headline from 116 to about 98 copies survived, the furnace result rests on a physically unsupported premise (offcuts to sheet), the part lists are invented where real open designs exist, and no recycling literature is cited. A recycling engineer would call it a tidy toy model that frames a good question (do the recyclers repay their own imports?) but cannot yet answer it.
